# A center of two limbs given to the constructor of a BallVector, each limb guarded

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `bv_center_entry_2` · proved for finite operands · proved for infinite and NaN operands · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

$c$, exactly:

$$z = c.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $c = c_0 + c_1$, $z = z_0 + z_1$.

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of the loop `bv_make_2_entry`, called by the constructors of `BallVector<T, 2, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 2>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $c$ is normalized: $c_0 = \mathrm{RN}(c_0 + c_1)$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $z$ is normalized: $z_0 = \mathrm{RN}(z_0 + z_1)$.
- $z = c$ exactly.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `bv_center_entry_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/BvNegMake.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/BvNegMake.v), against `bv_center_entry_2_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions bv_center_entry_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition bv_center_entry_2_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall c0 c1 : R,
  normalized_2 emin prec c0 c1 ->
  let '(z0, z1) := bv_center_entry_2 emin prec tie_even c0 c1 in
  normalized_2 emin prec z0 z1 /\
  (z0 + z1) = (c0 + c1).
```

## Infinite and NaN operands

The statement above is about finite operands. The claims also say what the kernel returns when its operands may be infinite or NaN. That statement requires:

- $c$ is canonical: finite and normalized, or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$, or $(\mathrm{NaN}, \mathrm{NaN})$.

and then:

- $z$ is canonical and is $c$ exactly: when $c$ is finite, $z$ is finite and normalized with $z_0 + z_1 = c$; when $c = \pm\infty$, $z = (\pm\infty, 0)$; when $c$ is a NaN, $z = (\mathrm{NaN}, \mathrm{NaN})$.
- When every operand and $z$ are finite, the statement on finite operands holds:
    - $z$ is normalized: $z_0 = \mathrm{RN}(z_0 + z_1)$.
    - $z = c$ exactly.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

**Status of this statement:** proved. Rocq checks the theorem `bv_center_entry_2_ieee_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBvNegMake.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBvNegMake.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions bv_center_entry_2_ieee_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proofs of `bv_center_entry_2_correct` and `bv_center_entry_2_ieee_correct` depend on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** bv_center_2 on the guarded limbs, a copy of a canonical pair (milestone2.md, BallVector, Values). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/bv_center_entry_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/bv_center_entry_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`bv_center_2`](bv_center_2.md).

```
# The step of bv_make_2_entry, the constructor of a BallVector with 2-limb centers that the program
# supplies, as two arrays of limbs or as Expansion<T, 2> objects whose limbs it may have written
# (milestone2.md, "BallVector", "Values"): each limb guarded (rule R3: the program may have written
# a product there, as for one limb, bv_center_entry_1), then copied (bv_center_2). A center must be
# canonical: the guard is the identity on a canonical pair as a value (a zero limb made +0, an
# infinity or a NaN staying what it is), so its claims are those of bv_center_2. A pair that is not
# normalized is not covered: its step would be make_2_limbs, which has no real-model statement.

g0       = guard(c0)
g1       = guard(c1)
(z0, z1) = bv_center_2(g0, g1)
```

## Measured

The stored brute-force runs of this kernel's code: the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound. A run is shown only if it ran the code the kernel has now: its generated C++ (scalar and packed, every kernel it calls inlined, with the functions it calls; comments left out) must be the same at the commit of the run, as the fingerprints in [`results/brute-code.json`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/results/brute-code.json) show ([How to read a page](reading.md#what-the-measured-numbers-are)).

**Milestone 2**: the supplementary run of commit `8ee5ed9`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#bv_center_entry_2)).
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | largest error / bound |
|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled, supplementary run: 90 runners on 3 machines | 100 800 000 | 0 | 0 (exact) |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled, supplementary run: 90 runners on 3 machines | 100 800 000 | 0 | 0 (exact) |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements of the statement on infinite and NaN operands.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
- Anything about an operand that is not normalized, which only limbs given by the program can make: `from_limbs` in a build without checks, `from_limbs_unchecked`, or `limb[]` written directly.
